pos.personaBrief: Highest possession in La Liga (66.5% after 22 games, 68.91% over 2025/26) and Flick's wish to be more direct; the team keeps the ball and does not give it away on purpose, though it accepted ceding it vs Bayern for vertical transitions.

pro.personaBrief: Possession build-up from the keeper (fewest long passes) but vertical, most through balls (218), balls in behind for wingers; Flick wants to reach goal faster.

est.personaBrief: Structured 4-3-3 with a mobile nine, wingers switching sides and eights between the lines; defined rest-defence but fluid roles in attack.

lar.personaBrief: Yamal holds the right width, Balde and Koundé advance, Raphinha on the left; wingers decisive, though eights feed the middle.

blo.personaBrief: Very high line near halfway, offside trap, counter-press, press high for 90 minutes; Flick refuses to defend low even after criticism.

mar.personaBrief: UEFA observers: back four use zonal marking in open play; offside line is space-based; corner marking undocumented, shorter defenders suggest zonal-leaning.

pla.personaBrief: Flick: we are Barca, we play our DNA, will not sit back or change out of fear; same high-line model against everyone, imposed from day one.

res.personaBrief: Flick loves the risky style and refuses to protect 1-0 leads, wants to impose play away too, yet the treble shows results matter.

sis.personaBrief: Strong collective system with pressing duties for all, yet Yamal and Raphinha get freedom within roles and mobility of the nine.

jog.personaBrief: Technical La Masia players (Pedri, Yamal, Cubarsi) but with aggressive intensity needed for the press; technique over pace in selection.

bas.personaBrief: Second-youngest team in La Liga, Yamal, Cubarsi, Balde, Casado, Bernal key; Flick integrates youngsters and academy players, title won with them.

lid.personaBrief: Flick: discipline is necessary, but open door and connecting with players; rewards hard work, equal rules, listens yet decides.
